summary: The EN tax return page sits at position 32 because it is written for people who have already chosen the service. It never answers the questions in the queries it is shown for: what a working holiday tax return is, whether you must lodge, the deadline, whether you can do it yourself, or what backpacker tax is. The home page, with the same keyword set and far more authority, holds the informational and comparison copy and links to /tax-return once with the anchor 'Tax Return'. The calculators link nowhere near it. The guide 'How to Lodge a Working Holiday Tax Return' targets the same phrase and also ranks around 30. The plan keeps the home page and the strong guides as they are, adds an answer-first definition, a neutral two-ways comparison, six FAQ items and visible TPB proof to /tax-return (DE and JA equivalents included), and wires home, calculator, the service row and the top guides to /tax-return with descriptive anchors. Two P1 hygiene items: the EN-only refund range sentence on /tax-return, and three EN decision guides with zero impressions that need an indexing check. Expect content alone to move /tax-return from page 4 to page 2. Reaching the top 5 for these competitive commercial queries will also need links from other sites.

2) 'If tax was withheld from your pay, you will usually need to lodge, and a lodged return is the only way tax withheld at the wrong rate is reconciled. findings.locator: const FAQS = [
findings.problem: The FAQ only covers the process after someone has chosen the service; it lacks the stand-alone questions people search and AI answers quote (must I lodge, can I do it myself, how much will I get, what is backpacker tax, can I lodge before I leave, who checks it).
findings.fix:
Append these items to FAQS (they flow into faqLd automatically):
1) Q 'Do working holiday makers have to lodge a tax return?' A 'Usually, yes. If tax was withheld from your pay in Australia you will generally need to lodge for that financial year, and lodging is the only way tax withheld at the wrong rate is reconciled. If you earned no Australian income at all, there is nothing to lodge.'
2) Q 'Can I do my working holiday tax return myself?' A 'Yes. Lodging through myGov is free, and for a simple year with one employer and your TFN on file from the first shift it can be straightforward. Residency, the Medicare levy and deductions are the questions to take care over, because the form accepts whatever answer you give.'
3) Q 'How much tax refund will I get on a working holiday visa?' A 'Nobody can say before your ATO record has been read. A refund is the gap between what was withheld and what you owed, so it depends on whether any weeks were taxed at 45%, whether the Medicare levy was charged when it should not have been, and what your work lets you deduct. The calculator gives an indicative figure.' (link 'calculator' to /calculator)
4) Q 'What is backpacker tax?' A 'The everyday name for the working holiday maker rates: 15% on the first $45,000 of income, then 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000 and 45% above $190,000. Whether those rates apply to your year depends on its facts and is for the ATO to decide.'
5) Q 'Can I lodge my tax return before I leave Australia?' A 'If you are leaving Australia permanently and will not earn Australian income again that year, an early return can be lodged before 30 June. Otherwise the return is lodged after the year ends on 30 June, from wherever you are.'
6) Q 'Is a registered tax agent involved?' A 'Yes. Working Holiday Tax operates under the supervision of a registered tax agent, and every return is reviewed and signed off by a registered tax agent before it is lodged with the ATO.'
findings.evidence: Facts from public/llms.txt Key facts (WHM rates, effective 1 July 2026, unchanged from 2025-26) and from existing site copy (early return on permanent departure: /blog/working-holiday-visa-tax-guide-417-462 and /blog/what-happens-without-your-tfn). findings.locator: タックスリターン代行｜申告書は登録タックスエージェントが確認して承認
findings.problem: Japanese commercial demand is almost all 'タックスリターン 税理士' (plus おすすめ, 安い, 費用, 帰国後) and is captured by the guide /ja/blog/what-is-a-tax-agent, while /ja/tax-return has 17 impressions and never explains who can lodge an Australian return; the bridge in the guide sits only in the last line.
findings.fix: On /ja/tax-return add a Section after 'ご用意いただくもの', title 'オーストラリアのタックスリターンは誰に頼めばいい？', copy: 'オーストラリアで報酬を受けて申告書を作成・提出できるのは、TPB（Tax Practitioners Board）に登録されたタックスエージェントです。日本の税理士資格だけでは、オーストラリアの申告書を有料で扱うことはできません。当社は登録タックスエージェントの監督のもとで運営しており、申告書は登録タックスエージェントが確認して承認してから、ATOに提出されます。料金は定額で、還付額に対する割合ではありません。' Rename the FAQ 'タックスリターンの提出期限はいつですか？' to 'タックスリターンはいつまでに提出すればいいですか？' (same answer). In /ja/blog/what-is-a-tax-agent, add to the end of the section '費用はどう考えればいいのか？': '当社の進め方と保証は[ワーホリのタックスリターン代行](/ja/tax-return)のページにまとめています。' Keep everything else in that guide (95 clicks, what works stays). No price figures.

findings.locator: A registered tax agent can see every employer who reported income against your TFN, not only the ones you remember.

findings.fix: Replace with: 'A registered tax agent works from the same ATO record you see in myGov, and checks each income statement against the jobs you remember, including ones an employer finalised late.'
findings.evidence: ATO pre-fill shows employer income statements in myTax once marked tax ready; the site's own /tax-return copy says the return is 'built from' that record.
